Every checker in the production verification pipeline appears here exactly once, with the exact line that wires it into each engine. parity.js asserts this list and the two shipped pipelines agree in BOTH directions, so a checker added to production and not registered here fails the suite; negative-control.js drives its removals from this list, so registering a checker is what puts it under negative-control coverage. Edit the pipelines and this file together.

_limits: The pipeline-to-registry sweep in parity.js recognises the two ordinary wiring shapes (a result concatenated directly, or parked in a local declared with it). Checkers wired unusually — inside a ternary, or assigned to a pre-declared local — are invisible to it and carry a note here. Wire new checks the ordinary way and the sweep will catch a missing registration for you.
